records.text: The Khazars were a nomadic Turkic tribe that adopted Judaism in the eighth century.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Khazars were a nomadic Turkic tribe who adopted Judaism in the 8th century.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Reference works describe the Khazars as a Turkic-speaking steppe polity whose ruling elite adopted Judaism, probably in the mid-to-late eighth century. Calling the entire people a nomadic tribe and implying population-wide conversion overstates a more complex polity and an elite-led, incompletely documented conversion.

sources.title: YIVO Encyclopedia: Khazaria
sources.relevance: Supports Turkic language and an eighth-century conversion among important segments of the Khazar elite while qualifying the statement's broader wording.

records.text: Abraham Polak wrote a researched book arguing that Israelis descend from the Khazar tribe that converted to Judaism.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: But if you read books that were printed in Israel by the Israelis, they themselves declared that they were Khazarian. You could look at a guy named Abraham Polak as an example, who wrote a book, did all the research, was awarded for his research, and said, hey, we're that tribe.

verification.notes: Poliak's book and contemporary discussion support his Khazar-origin hypothesis for much of Eastern European Jewry, but the statement overgeneralizes this into a claim about Israelis as a whole.

sources.title: You Don't Have to Be Khazarian? | The New York Review of Books
sources.relevance: Describes Poliak's argument that Khazars were ancestors of much of Eastern European Jewry.

sources.title: Khazaria: History of a Jewish Kingdom in Europe | National Library of Israel
sources.relevance: Authoritative catalog record for Abraham Poliak's book.

records.text: Owens claimed that Russia and Persia brought an end to the Khazar Khaganate.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: That's why they have deep hatred for Russia because Russia put an end to the Khazarian Empire. So my conspiracy theory to jump onto yours is that they're doing all of this and then they're going to take Russia. Like Russia is they've got beef with actually it was two countries that took out the Khazarian Empire. It was Russia and Persia.

verification.notes: Modern scholarship attributes the Khazar Khaganates fall to Rus aggression together with pressure from Pechenegs, Oghuz Turks, Volga Bulgaria, and shifting trade routes. Persia was not one of the powers that ended the tenth-century Khazar state; earlier Persian-Khazar conflicts belonged to a different era.

sources.title: The Khazars
sources.relevance: Oxford history attributes the fall to Rus, Pecheneg, Oghuz, and trade-route pressures, not Persia.

sources.title: Khazars
sources.relevance: Encyclopaedia Iranica distinguishes earlier Persian relations from the later Rus-led fall of Khazaria.

records.text: Owens claimed that modern Israel is a reassembled Khazar Khaganate and that its people are not the Jews of the Bible.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: These are the facts. This is the Khazarian Empire. they are reassembled that's what israel is they have never they are not jewish they are not the jews of the bible

verification.notes: The claim that modern Israel is a reassembled Khazar state and its Jews are not descended from historical Jewish populations is directly contradicted by population-genetic research. Genome-wide studies find Ashkenazi Jews derive primarily from Middle Eastern and European populations, share ancestry with other Jewish populations, and show no significant Khazar or north-Caucasus contribution. Israel also includes many non-Ashkenazi Jewish populations, making the blanket claim still broader and less accurate.

sources.title: No evidence from genome-wide data of a Khazar origin for the Ashkenazi Jews
sources.relevance: Peer-reviewed genome-wide study directly rejects significant Khazar origin and finds shared Middle Eastern and Jewish ancestry.

sources.title: Abrahams Children in the Genome Era
sources.relevance: Genome-wide analysis finds distinct Jewish population clusters with shared Middle Eastern ancestry and variable admixture.
